intro: Purpose beyond para que: formal connectors, a que after verbs of movement, and no sea que.

palabras.consejo: It takes the subjunctive and two different subjects: «a fin de que todos lo entiendan».
Like «a fin de que»: subjunctive and another subject. With the same subject: «con el fin de» + infinitive.
It is very formal, from documents. It takes the subjunctive: «con el objeto de que nadie falte».
It goes with a noun or an infinitive: «con vistas a mejorar». The v sounds b.
It takes the subjunctive and warns of a danger: «llévate el paraguas, no sea que llueva».
It takes an infinitive if the subject is the same: «a fin de ahorrar». With another subject: «a fin de que».
It is written with y: a-yun-ta-MYEN-to. It is where city paperwork is done.
«Tomar medidas» means to take action. It also means size: «¿qué medida tiene?».
The v sounds b. A noun or an infinitive follows: «evitar el tráfico», «evitar llegar tarde».
It comes from «mejor». The j sounds like a strong h: me-ho-RAR.
It comes from «paso». You say «pasear por el parque». It has two vowels together: pa-se-AR.
The feminine is «vecina». In Spain the c sounds «th»: be-THI-no.
Feminine plural of «vario». The v sounds like b: BA-rias.
Plural of «medida». In «tomar medidas» it means taking action.
Future of «cerrar», to close. The c before e is th, and rr is strong.
Subjunctive of «poder», to be able. The ue is a diphthong: PWE-dan.
Plural of «autobús», bus. Stress on BU.
Subjunctive of «necesitar», to need. The c before e is th: ne-the-SI-te.
Plural of «técnico». The accent falls on the e, which is stressed: TEK-ni-kos.
Future of «ir», to go. The accent falls on RAN: i-RAN.
Plural of «barrio», a neighbourhood. The rr is strong: BA-rryos.
Subjunctive of «contar», to tell. The ue is a diphthong: KWEN-ten.
Plural of «fiesta», a celebration. The ie is a diphthong: FIES-tas.
Plural of «atasco», a traffic jam. Stress on TAS.
Subjunctive of «salir», to go out. Stress on SAL: SAL-gan.
Subjunctive of «encontrar», to find. The ue is a diphthong.
Feminine plural of «cortado», cut or blocked. Stress on TA.
Subjunctive of «entender», to understand. The ie is a diphthong.
Imperative of «llevarse», to take away. The ll sounds like y: YE-ba-te.
Plural of «motor», engine. Stress on TO: mo-TO-res.
From «salir», to go out. Stress on SA: SA-len.
From «perseguir», to chase. The gu before i is silent: per-SI-ge.
Past participle of «colocar», to place. The c before o is k: ko-lo-KA-do.
From «oler», but the o becomes «hue»: «huele», «huelo». The h is silent.
Plural of «terraza». The rr at the start of the middle syllable is strong.
Plural of «vaso», a glass. The v sounds like b: BA-sos.
Participle of «devolver», to give back. The ue is a diphthong: de-BWEL-to.
Plural of «mayor». Here it means older people. Stress on YO.
Plural of «banco». Here it means a bench, not a bank.
Subjunctive of «romper», to break. Stress on ROM.
Here it means a magical atmosphere. The ch sounds like ch in «chico».
Plural of «sujeto», the subject of a sentence. The j sounds like h.
Plural of «distinto», different. Stress on TIN: dis-TIN-tos.
Past tense of «tomar», to take. Stress on MA: to-MA-ron.
Subjunctive of «ocurrir», to happen. The rr is strong: o-KU-rra.
From «venir», to come. The v sounds like b: BEN-go.
Subjunctive of «explicar», to explain. The x sounds like ks.
«Esto» refers to something unnamed close to you. It has no accent.

texto:
With **one subject**, purpose is a preposition + **infinitive**: **para**, **a fin de**, **con el fin de**, **con el objeto de**, **con vistas a**.

With **two subjects**, add **que** + **subjunctive**: **para que**, **a fin de que**, **con el fin de que**, **con el objeto de que**.

The tense follows the main verb: lo **hago** para que **estés** contento; lo **hice** para que **estuvieras** contento.

After a verb of movement (ir, venir, salir, subir…) Spanish uses **a**: vengo **a** verte; vengo **a que** me **expliques** esto.

**No sea que** + subjunctive warns of something bad you want to avoid: llévate el paraguas, **no sea que llueva**.

**¿Para qué?** asks for the purpose. **¿Por qué?** asks for the cause.

**One subject → infinitive**:

- para + infinitive
- a fin de + infinitive
- con el objeto de + infinitive
- ir / venir a + infinitive

**Two subjects → que + subjunctive**:

- para que + subjunctive
- a fin de que + subjunctive
- con el objeto de que + subjunctive
- ir / venir a que + subjunctive

To avoid a danger: **no sea que** + subjunctive.

ejemplos.estudio: Lo hice para que estuvieras contento.
ejemplos.alumno: I did it so that you would be happy.
analisis: Lo hice para que estuvieras contento

ejemplos.estudio: Habla despacio con el fin de que todos te entiendan.
ejemplos.alumno: Speak slowly so that everybody understands you.
analisis: Habla despacio con el fin de que todos te entiendan
con el fin de que todos te entiendan

ejemplos.estudio: Llévate el paraguas, no sea que llueva.
ejemplos.alumno: Take the umbrella, in case it rains.
analisis: Llévate el paraguas no sea que llueva

pregunta.texto: When is «a fin de que» used?

opciones.texto: cuando el sujeto es el mismo
opciones.explicacion: Then «a fin de» + infinitive is enough.
Well done: with another subject you need «que» + subjunctive.
It works in any tense; what matters is the subjects.

pregunta.texto: Complete with one subject: infinitive or «que»?

frase.texto: Tomaron medidas a fin de ____ el tráfico.

piezas.traduccion: Tomaron medidas a fin de ____ el tráfico.

opciones.explicacion: That is it: the same subject asks for the infinitive.
«Que» needs another subject and here there is only one.
It is a conjugated verb. With one subject the infinitive goes.

frase.texto: Cerrarán el centro para que los vecinos puedan pasear

piezas.traduccion: The centre will be closed so that residents can walk around

pregunta.texto: What does «no sea que llueva» express?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: it warns of something you want to avoid.
That would be «dado que». «No sea que» is a precaution.
It expresses no wish, but prevention of a danger.

pregunta.texto: Write in Spanish: «in case it rains».
Choose what follows «vengo» with another subject.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: after a verb of movement, «a que» + subjunctive.
«Por que» would express the cause, not the purpose.
«De que» is not used for purpose after «vengo».

pregunta.texto: Which one asks about the purpose?

opciones.explicacion: It asks about the cause, not the purpose.
Correct: «para» looks ahead, to the aim.
